details.title: Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2
details.detailText:
By May 2019

Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2

Technology · United States; Taiwan

Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2, model GG2; enterprise assisted-reality wearable. Excludes Explorer Edition and Enterprise Edition 1.

Optics & glass
Materials

Why this date

Available for purchase by May 2019. Community: Enterprise customers purchasing through Google’s sales or partner channel. Google dates launch to May; 20 May begins contact with sales/partners and a 21 May trade report says partner availability.

The mark is an upper date limit for the stated entry claim. Earlier entry remains unresolved.

Direct evidence.

The May 2019 enterprise-channel offer and 21 May partner-availability report support availability by that time; direct developer resellers came later in 2020.

The event is month-precision and does not prove first transaction, availability in every market, or direct reseller purchase in May 2019.

Scope: regions unspecified. Applications: Hands-free enterprise work. Population: not yet researched. Market: Businesses purchasing through solution partners.

Scoped configuration: Glass Enterprise Edition 2 partner offer reported in May 2019; first commercial-offer date not established.

First commercial availability: unknown; applicability: applicable.

Historical claim: accepted. Lifecycle classification: accepted.

A May 2019 enterprise partner offer and a February 2020 direct-reseller offer are documented. Purchase quantities and the dates of first offers are unknown; prior private arrangements were not excluded.

Entry evidence

Glass Enterprise Edition 2: faster and more helpful · 20 May 2019, final paragraph

Invites businesses to contact sales or solution partners starting that day.

Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2 resurrects AR for Google · 21 May 2019, final paragraph

Reports EE2 available for business through third-party partners with MSRP $999.

Glass Enterprise Edition 2 now available for developers · 4 February 2020, second paragraph

Dates launch to previous May and describes a new direct reseller channel for developers.

Lifecycle dates and unknowns
Recorded events

commercial offer · May 2019

Google announced Glass Enterprise Edition 2 on 20 May 2019 and invited enterprise customers to contact its sales team or partners; a 21 May report described partner availability.

commercial offer · 4 February 2020

On 4 February 2020 Google said developers and businesses could purchase Glass Enterprise Edition 2 devices directly from named hardware resellers.

withdrawal · By 15 March 2023

By 15 March 2023 Google was no longer selling Glass Enterprise Edition, including Edition 2; reseller withdrawal and last actual device use are not established.

support end · 15 September 2023

Google identified a support and replacement cutoff for Glass Enterprise Edition.

documented description · 8 August 2018

The test laboratory received a Glass Enterprise Edition 2 GG2 sample.

Sources
Electromagnetic Emissions Compliance Report E2/2018/80047 (2018)

details.title: B-DNA helical constraints
details.detailText:
1953-4-25

B-DNA helical constraints

Science · King’s College London, England

Awareness proxy

Franklin and Gosling inferred a probable helix, approximately 34 Å repeat and 20 Å diameter, with exterior phosphates and a probable two-chain unit.

Genetics

Built on
Humidity-varied DNA diffraction
1953

Hydration-dependent fibre diffraction supplied the patterns from which Franklin and Gosling inferred B-form geometry.

Linked events: demonstration (by 1953) → dated assertion (by Apr 1953).

Earlier exposures and subsequent interpretation overlap in the evidence; the inference was documented by 1953, without an established date of first formulation.

Why this date

Publication used as an awareness estimate. Community: DNA structural researchers reading Nature. Date of the cited public report or documented event.

Awareness proxy.

The Nature paper exposed the qualified inferences to the structural-biology literature rather than using the earlier undated inference.

The article is a documented route to specialist awareness; later adoption of this exact bundle was not established.

Publication does not prove other scientists agreed with every part, nor establish earliest external exposure.

Scope: regions unspecified. Applications: unspecified. Population: not yet researched. Market: not yet researched.

First commercial availability: not applicable; applicability: not applicable.

Historical claim: accepted. Lifecycle classification: needs review.

The authors did not call diffraction alone direct proof of helicity or offer a complete structure; the model involved additional density and chemical arguments.

Entry evidence

Molecular Configuration in Sodium Thymonucleate · Nature 171, pp. 740–741, complete article and issue date

Public scientific account of B-form dimensions and qualified helix and chain interpretation.

Lifecycle dates and unknowns
Recorded events

dated assertion · by Apr 1953

Franklin and Gosling inferred a probable helix, approximately 34 Å repeat and 20 Å diameter, with exterior phosphates and a probable two-chain unit.

publication · 1953-4-25

Franklin and Gosling published their qualified B-form structural interpretation in Nature.

Sources
Molecular Configuration in Sodium Thymonucleate (1953)

details.title: Photolithographic diffusion windows
details.detailText:
By 1958

Photolithographic diffusion windows

Technology · Bell Laboratories, New Jersey, United States

Scoped inference

Jules Andrus and Walter Bond adapted photoresist patterning to etch windows in silicon oxide before localized diffusion.

Semiconductors

Built on
Silicon oxide diffusion mask
By 1955

Andrus and Bond applied photoresist patterning to Frosch and Derick’s oxide-mask process.

Linked events: dated assertion (1955) → dated assertion (1955).

Both nodes are 1955; the source states the dependency, so year-level overlap is not a reversed chronology.

Why this date

Use contextually inferred by 1958. Community: Fairchild mesa-transistor fabrication engineers. Latest documented community-use or recognition bound; no earliest date is established.

The mark is an upper date limit for the stated entry claim. Earlier entry remains unresolved.

Scoped contextual inference.

Moore’s contemporary-participant account connects Fairchild photolithography, oxide-masked mesa emitters and 1958 shipments, providing earlier real specialist use than the 1964 patent.

The dated use follows from linked passages on the Fairchild process and 1958 shipments; it does not assert identical Bell masks or an independently demonstrated first use.

The Fairchild method is contextual evidence of use of the same general patterned oxide-window process; the source does not identify every original Bell mask or prove exact transfer of a physical tool.

Scope: California, United States. Applications: transistor emitter diffusion. Population: not yet researched. Market: not yet researched.

Scoped configuration: Fairchild’s photoresist-patterned silicon-oxide openings used to delimit diffusion in mesa transistor fabrication; individual masks need not be identical to the earlier Bell Labs masks.

First commercial availability: not yet researched; applicability: not yet assessed.

Historical claim: accepted. Lifecycle classification: needs review.

This node is not Fairchild’s later step-and-repeat camera or DOFL’s separate diode-array work.

Entry evidence

The Role of Fairchild in Silicon Technology · Printed pp. 54–58, photolithography, early mesa transistors and oxide-masked emitter diffusion

Moore describes photoresist and oxide openings, Fairchild’s mesa emitter diffusion, and 100 early 2N696 shipments in 1958.

Lifecycle dates and unknowns
Recorded events

dated assertion · 1955

Jules Andrus and Walter Bond adapted photoresist patterning to etch windows in silicon oxide before localized diffusion.

publication · 1964-03-03

Andrus issued patent publicly described photoresist-patterned windows in silicon oxide for selective diffusion.

practical use · by 1958

Fairchild used photolithographic oxide-window fabrication in its mesa transistor work and shipped 100 2N696 transistors by 1958.

Sources
1955: Photolithography Techniques Are Used to Make Silicon Devices (not specified in preserved source metadata)
The Role of Fairchild in Silicon Technology (1998)
Fabrication of semiconductor devices (1964)
